beats.text: Here is what I would do, in order, and where each one meets the earlier **parts**.
First, **check** whether it fits. Pasting twenty-three thousand tokens beat every tool setup I built.
If it does not fit, use the **cheapest** tool that works, like grep, then page the file. That is the rule from Part **eight**: plain code first, then a small model, then a language model.
Pass **paths** only when results are big, and give a sub-agent a **narrow** brief. It is Part seven's split again: code owns the order, the model owns the judgment.
And **look** at individual answers, because that is how I found my own bug. Part eight had one too.
Three things I did not test: **skills**, **injection**, and stale documents. They belong to the later Deep Agents and security posts.
